subject: Clarification: Cloud provider SOC coverage for subprocessor / audit window
messages:
From: R. Douglas <security@finovahealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 evidence + cloud provider carve-out question

Hi Jasmine,

We're working toward our vendor assessment for the October renewal and need to confirm a couple of items before we sign the PO:

1) Could you provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report for the period covering Apr 2025 - Mar 2026 (or the nearest available period)?
2) Our auditors asked whether your cloud provider's SOC reports are included in Redwood's scope or if Redwood performs a "carve-out" / subservice exclusion. Specifically, can you confirm whether OrionCloud (your infra subprocessor) is treated as a subservice organization with a carve-out, or if their controls are mapped into Redwood's SOC coverage?
3) Relatedly, do you maintain an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and can you confirm whether any changes to subprocessors occurred in the audit window?

If you have a bridge letter template (or can provide a statement that the control coverage remains materially consistent since the report date), that would accelerate our procurement review.

Thanks — we need to get this to our internal audit by Oct 20.

Regards,
R. Douglas
Security & Privacy Manager
Finova Health
attachments: none

From: k. iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: R. Douglas <security@finovahealth.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence + cloud provider carve-out question

Hi R,

Thanks for the note. Looping in Jasmine who owns the account and Neha from InfoSec for a confirmed response. Quick answers while we pull the artifacts:

- We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report for the most recent audit period.
- Redwood treats major cloud infra providers (we use OrionCloud as an example in some regions) as subservice organizations. The primary approach for that provider is to rely on their SOC report where applicable, and we map shared controls in our subservice responsibility matrix rather than fully absorbing their controls into Redwood's report. We will clarify whether OrionCloud was in-scope or carved out for the Apr 2025 - Mar 2026 window.
- We maintain a subprocessor registry; there were two minor subprocessor changes during the audit window (one replaced, one added) — we'll provide the inventory and change log.

Jasmine / Neha: can you share the SOC report and a draft bridge letter we can send to Finova?

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Manager, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: R. Douglas <security@finovahealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence + cloud provider carve-out question

Hi Robert — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the SOC 2 Type II we can share and a subservice mapping spreadsheet that shows how we treated major providers during the audit period. See the key points below: 

- Attachment: redwood-soc2-type2-2026.pdf (covers audit period 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31).
- Attachment: redwood-subservice-mapping-2026.xlsx (lists subprocessors, last change dates, and whether the provider was treated as a carve-out or included).
- For the Apr 2025 - Mar 2026 audit: OrionCloud is listed as a subservice organization with a carve-out for infrastructure-level controls (networking, physical data center controls). We documented the shared responsibility mapping for logical access, encryption, and patching where Redwood retained operational control; those controls are tested in Redwood's SOC testing matrix.
- Subprocessor changes during the window: DataStream Inc. (log aggregation) was added 2025-11-02; Backuply (backup vendor) replaced an internal tool on 2026-02-10. Both are noted in the spreadsheet; neither triggered a material exception in the SOC report.

Bridge letter: we do not have a one-size-fits-all signed bridge letter in every case, but we can provide a statement of continuity / bridge letter confirming there have been no material control changes since the report date that would affect the covered criteria. If Finova needs a vendor-signed attestation referencing specific controls, please let us know which control families are most important (e.g., CC6 logical access, CC7 change management) and we'll tailor it.

Next steps requested from you: confirm whether your audit team requires a formal signed bridge letter (and if so which control families), or whether a documented statement plus the subservice mapping will suffice. We can turn around a draft within 2 business days.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence + cloud provider carve-out question

Thanks Jasmine — that's very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our audit team: 

- They want explicit confirmation that OrionCloud's SOC report covers the OrionCloud regions used by Redwood for Finova's data (us-west-2). Can you confirm region alignment?
- They also asked whether Redwood's SOC tests included vendor control evidence from OrionCloud (i.e., did the auditor review OrionCloud's SOC report as part of Redwood's subservice testing) or if Redwood's testing was limited to your control mappings and compensating controls.

On the bridge letter: our preferred path is a short signed attestation that there have been no material control changes since the report date that would affect CC6 and CC7. If you can provide the attestation along with the mapping, that should satisfy the audit window.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we still aim to submit the package by Oct 20.

Regards,
Rob

2) Auditor scope note: Our auditor did review OrionCloud's SOC reporting as part of Redwood's subservice evidence collection; the SOC report is referenced in Redwood's audit working papers. We'll provide a short note from Neha confirming that (see draft below).

3) Bridge letter: We'll provide a signed attestation addressing CC6 and CC7 continuity. Draft will be attached and we can sign it once you confirm it meets Finova's requirements.

Draft wording (for your review):
"Redwood Inference attests that, to the best of our knowledge, there have been no material changes to controls covering logical access (CC6) and change management (CC7) since the SOC 2 Type II report dated 2026-03-31 that would materially affect the covered criteria for Finova Health."

If that looks good, we will: (a) have Neha produce a 1-paragraph auditor-scope confirmation, (b) finalize the attestation for signature, and (c) attach the OrionCloud SOC reference and the redwood-subservice-mapping-2026.xlsx.

We aim to send the full package by EOD Wed (Oct 20) which should meet your audit submission timeline.
